provenance.l: Mars Pathfinder EDL (Braun et al., AIAA 97-3663) — entry at 133 km, 7,479 m/s relative at −13.65°, 585.3 kg, β 62.4 kg/m²; chute 171 s after entry at about 9 km (Fig. 7); heat shield 22 s and bridle 41 s after the chute; radar lock about 1.5 km; airbags at about 300 m (296 s); RAD ignition 300 s at 50–70 m (60 m drawn, an estimate); bridle cut 21 m above the surface; first impact 306 s; bounced more than 15 times. The chute drag area (70 m²) is fitted to the 135 s from chute to first impact
Pathfinder landing accelerations (JPL PIA00797) — first two impacts 6 s apart, which the caption converts to a 16.7 m bounce; 15 bounces shown, then about a minute more of bouncing and rolling
MER landing press kit (2004), p. 32 — Pathfinder rolled to a stop about 1 km from first impact, about 2.5 minutes after it (a comparison remark; the roll distance is drawn as an estimate)
Mars Pathfinder mission (PDS) — landing 16:56:55 UTC, petals fully deployed 18:24 UTC, about 87 minutes later
Mars Pathfinder EDL — Golombek et al. (1997)
